sentences.text: Hardness crept up to 240 ppm overnight — someone check whether the crushed coral bag split. Honestly, half our overtime comes from grinding out sloppy tack welds the day shift leaves behind. Dim lights keep the wild bettas calm, so we work by headlamp when netting out pairs. Third rejection this week on bay two's seams—somebody check that wire feed. Nobody warned me that angelfish eat their first three clutches before figuring out parenthood. Her ultrasonic probe traced the seam twice; the second pass found the void the first had missed. I mark each spawning jar's lid with tape: date, pair number, hardness at laying. Sparks rained off the hull plate while two welders argued, through their visors, about last night's match. Eggs stuck to the heater cord again, which means scraping and praying half survive the move. Under the floodlights, the half-finished chassis looked less like a war machine and more like a beached steel whale. He logs GH and KH in a spiral notebook, one column per shelf, dated in pencil. The shift supervisor taped the rejection slip to the chassis and told nobody to touch it until the metallurgist arrived. Every runt gets fed to the bichir; sentiment doesn't pay for fish food. All armored side panels shall be degreased, inspected for lamination defects, and logged before entering the assembly line. Her ledger shows which pairings threw long fins and which threw nothing worth keeping. Nine bare chassis sat in line for turret installation, but only one crane operator was scheduled before noon. Fry from batch eleven took powdered egg yolk at dawn and again at three. Quality inspectors rejected fourteen hull plates on Tuesday after ultrasonic testing revealed porosity along the lower weld seams. Records indicate the corydoras deposited eggs on the glass within six hours of the cool-water change. A hairline crack in the mantlet casting sent the whole batch back to the foundry, three weeks of schedule gone. What is the meaning of the word tank?
